hints.title: Recursive Base Extension
hints.text: A pyramid of height h requires that the three sub-pyramid positions on the next row each support height at least h - 1.

hints.title: Height State Transition
hints.text: For normal pyramids, dp[r][c] = min(dp[r+1][c-1], dp[r+1][c], dp[r+1][c+1]) + 1 whenever grid[r][c] is fertile.

hints.title: Bidirectional Evaluation
hints.text: Apply the recurrence from bottom to top for regular pyramids, and from top to bottom for inverse pyramids.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: The max pyramid height at (r, c) depends on min of three adjacent cells in row r + 1.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Verifying every possible pyramid expansion independently takes O(M * N * min(M, N)^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing pyramid heights per cell in a 2D table allows computing both normal and inverse pyramids in linear grid time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should formulate the transition min(dp[r+1][c-1], dp[r+1][c], dp[r+1][c+1]) + 1.
